name: Arm Holdings
description: Arm designs processor architectures and pre-built circuit blocks (CPU cores, and increasingly GPU, system and platform IP) that chip companies license to build into their own products, rather than manufacturing or selling physical chips itself. It earns money two ways: upfront and ongoing licensing fees for access to its architecture and designs, and per-unit royalties paid on every chip that ships containing Arm technology, so revenue scales with the enormous volume of Arm-based chips shipped annually across smartphones, PCs, automotive, IoT and a fast-growing data-center/AI infrastructure market. Arm's architecture underpins the vast majority of the world's smartphone application processors and is expanding into servers, PCs and AI infrastructure, competing against the incumbent x86 architecture (Intel/AMD) and the free, open-source RISC-V architecture.

employees.asOf: FY2025 (year ended 2025-03-31), average headcount for the year

businessLines.name: Licensing and other revenue
businessLines.description: Upfront and ongoing fees for architecture/technology licenses, plus revenue from development tools and services; increasingly includes higher-value 'Arm Total Access' and Arm Flexible Access subscription-style licensing arrangements.

businessLines.name: Royalty revenue
businessLines.description: Per-chip royalties earned on Arm-based chips shipped by licensees across smartphones, embedded/IoT, automotive, networking, and a growing base of servers/AI infrastructure and PCs.
